start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.
start.defaults.cfg:
# values used when a profile never sets the key (or unsets it)
queue_depth = 325
log_budget = 330
retry_limit = 176
pool_size = 984
page_size = 780
cache_ttl = 239

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

# values used when a profile never sets the key (or unsets it)
http_timeout = 240
flush_ms = 757
pool_size = 948
batch_rows = 570
retry_limit = 682
cache_ttl = 861

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

http_timeout = 547
cache_ttl = 299

log_budget = 116

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

# values used when a profile never sets the key (or unsets it)
http_timeout = 187
shard_count = 397
log_budget = 562
pool_size = 937
flush_ms = 702
cache_ttl = 146

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

retry_limit = 265
flush_ms = 771
shard_count = 409

batch_rows = 556

prompt: Could you help me with something? What is the effective value of `flush_ms` for the `ibex6` profile in the `dev` environment? README.md has the resolution rules. Show me which file you got it from.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

shard_count = 363

flush_ms = 926

batch_rows = 920
queue_depth = 375

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

start.README.md:
# Profiles

`defaults.cfg` gives the base value of every key. A profile in `profiles/` is resolved for an environment like this:

1. resolve each profile named in `extends = a, b, ...` first, in the order listed (a later parent overrides an earlier one);
2. then apply the profile's own top-level `key = value` lines, then the `[env NAME]` section for the requested environment (if
   it has one); within a profile later lines win;
3. `unset key` takes the key back to its value in `defaults.cfg` at that point (later settings can still override it).

A parent is resolved for the same environment as its child. The effective value of a key is its resolved value, or the
`defaults.cfg` value if nothing set it.

flush_ms = 849
log_budget = 819

retry_limit = 427
cache_ttl = 238
